name: setup
context_rationale: Interactive, side-effecting dependency doctor: streams live pip + code-review-graph output to the user, prints a status report, may STOP and ask (no interpreter resolvable / target not a git repo), and writes repo-root side-effects (.mcp.json, .gitignore, .code-review-graph/) in the user's cwd. disable-model-invocation (user-only, never auto-run). All of this needs the parent conversation's tool access, visible terminal, and cwd - not a forked subagent. Logic lives in scripts/setup.py; the SKILL.md bash is a one-line $PYX bootstrap.
summary: One-shot dependency doctor + installer for the AI SDLC pipeline. A tiny bash bootstrap resolves a working Python 3 ($PYX), then hands all work to scripts/setup.py: install the runtime deps (PyYAML + code-review-graph) into it with VISIBLE streaming progress, verify them, register the code-review-graph MCP server for Claude Code (project .mcp.json, gitignored because the abs interpreter path is machine-specific), build the code graph, and print a status report plus the exact next steps (restart Claude Code + approve the MCP trust prompt). Idempotent - installs only what is missing. Fixes the silent/opaque first-run SessionStart-hook install by doing it interactively where the user can see it. The visible-install counterpart to the probe-and-nudge SessionStart hook (hooks/setup_env.py).

outputs.purpose: Register the code-review-graph MCP server for Claude Code (project-scoped stdio config; absolute interpreter path). Skipped by --no-mcp.
Append .mcp.json so the machine-specific absolute interpreter path it carries never commits.
Build the code graph so the CRG MCP server + CLI have data to serve. Skipped by --no-graph.

tools.name: setup
tools.purpose: The whole skill body in Python (os/pathlib/subprocess - no bash-on-Windows path/encoding/quoting traps): resolve sys.executable, install PyYAML + code-review-graph (streaming, visible), verify imports, register the CRG MCP server, gitignore .mcp.json, build the graph, print a status table + next steps. --check prints current toolchain state without changes (used for the live-state injection).

tools.name: code-review-graph
tools.purpose: Installed by setup (pip), then driven to register the project-scoped MCP server (writes .mcp.json) and build the code graph (.code-review-graph/) so the MCP tools + CLI have data.
tools.note: External pip package (github.com/tirth8205/code-review-graph), MCP-native; intentionally not bundled in the plugin.

harness_tools.name: Bash
